## Changes

Issue #241 is done for my slice. `Lifecycle.ts` no longer uses `Date`, `Date.UTC`, `Date.now`, or `Intl`, and the `globalDate` override is gone. All exported names and signatures are unchanged. Nothing was committed, and git, the ledger JSON, `apps/web/**`, `Organization.ts`, and `.githooks/` were not touched.

- **`packages/domain/src/rounds/Lifecycle.ts`**: removed the diagnostic line and added `import * as DateTime from "effect/DateTime"`. I rewrote `localToUtc`, `nextWeekdayDate` (through a private `nextWeekdayOn` on `DateTime.Utc`), `nextEightWeeksCadenceDates`, `addDays`, `teamToday`, and `calculateResultsReadyDeliveryTime`. `parseDateIso` and `formatDateIso` are unchanged. `formatDateIso` is now unused inside the module but stays exported, as the brief requires.
- **`packages/domain/src/rounds/Lifecycle.test.ts`**: added the characterization tests before refactoring. They pass on the old code and on the new code.
- **`packages/domain/src/rounds/TeamOverview.test.ts`**: removed the override. The fixture now uses `DateTime.add(DateTime.makeUnsafe({year:2025,month:1,day:6}), {days: 7*week})`. The timing measurement uses `DateTime.toEpochMillis(DateTime.nowUnsafe())`, and its comment is updated.
- **`packages/api/src/registry.privacy.test.ts`**: removed the override. The fixture date now uses `DateTime`.
- **`packages/cloudflare/src/PastRounds.test.ts`**: removed both `globalDate` overrides. I also replaced `Date.UTC` and the `toISOString().slice` calls with `DateTime`, since the brief lists `Date.UTC` for removal. The `nodeBuiltinImport` override stays.

The DateTime calls used for zone conversion:
- Wall clock to instant: `DateTime.toEpochMillis(DateTime.makeZonedUnsafe({ year, month, day, hour, minute }, { timeZone, adjustForTimeZone: true, disambiguation: "compatible" }))`. The brief wrote `hours`/`minutes`, but `Partial<Parts>` uses `hour`/`minute`, so I used those.
- Instant to zone parts: `DateTime.toParts(DateTime.makeZonedUnsafe(nowMs, { timeZone }))`.
- UTC calendar math: `DateTime.makeUnsafe({year,month,day})`, `DateTime.getPartUtc(from, "weekDay")`, `DateTime.add(utc, {days})`, `DateTime.formatIsoDateUtc`.

`"compatible"` is the default. I did not assume it: the characterization tests pin the expected values, and the planted-bug run below confirms the test catches a change to it.

## Characterization values (old code and new code agree)

- Berlin gap 2026-03-29 02:30 gives `2026-03-29T01:30:00Z` (later instant).
- Berlin overlap 2026-10-25 02:30 gives `2026-10-25T00:30:00Z` (earlier instant). Berlin 03:00 the same day gives `02:00Z`.
- New York gap 2026-03-08 02:30 gives `2026-03-08T07:30:00Z`.
- New York overlap 2026-11-01 01:30 gives `2026-11-01T05:30:00Z`.
- Results-ready, Berlin: 2026-03-28 20:00Z gives `2026-03-29T06:00Z`. 2026-03-29 06:30Z is immediate. 2026-10-25 06:30Z gives `2026-10-25T07:00Z`. 2026-10-25 20:00Z gives `2026-10-26T07:00Z`. The Nov 9 before-08, within-day, and after-20 cases were already pinned in the existing test.
- Cadence across the year boundary, instant 2026-12-31T23:30Z: `thursday` in Asia/Tokyo gives 2027-01-07 through 2027-02-25. In UTC it gives 2026-12-31 through 2027-02-18.

There were 22,000 random instant cases for results-ready, cadence, `nextRoundSlot`, and `nextWeekdayDate`. Zero mismatches. The only failures were the 5 s default Vitest timeout on that long scratch run.
